Ashoka's patronage turns Buddhism from a regional sect into a pan-Asian religion.
Kanishka's Fourth Buddhist Council leads to the split into Hinayana and Mahayana.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming Buddhism and Jainism completely rejected the caste system; they critiqued the Varna hierarchy but did not abolish it.
Confusing Mahayana Buddhism with Vedic influence; while Mahayana incorporated idol worship, its metaphysics remains distinct from Vedic pantheism.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Gangetic Plains: Core zone of origin.
  • Urbanization: Linked with trade routes.

Personalities

  • Mahavira: 24th Tirthankara.
  • Buddha: Shakyamuni.
  • Ashoka: The great propagator.

Core Contributions Mindmap

  • Social Impact
    • Promoted equality for Shudras and Women.
    • Challenged Brahminical hegemony.
  • Economic Impact
    • Ahimsa fostered non-violent trade culture.
    • Banking and guilds (Shrenis) patronized.
  • Architectural/Artistic Legacy
    • Stupas (Sanchi, Bharhut).
    • Chaityas and Viharas (Ajanta, Ellora).
    • Gandhara and Mathura Art schools.
